title: kbmon live view: ANSI redraw in place on macOS, Linux and Windows, plain frames on a pipe or NO_COLOR
goal: kbmon.py lays every frame out as the layout in this item's notes gives it: a header line, the alert line first while an alert is shown, each panel's title line at column 0 in the order kb, coord, sessions, querylog, host, sprint, log and its body rows, which its own mon_ module renders, behind a two-column gutter, with no line longer than the terminal's columns less one; on a terminal or with --ansi it redraws the frame in place every --interval seconds (1 to 300, default 5) with the ANSI cursor-home and erase sequences until Ctrl-C or --count frames and exits 0; on Windows mon_view.enable_vt() turns on the console's virtual terminal processing and kbmon writes plain frames when it returns False; NO_COLOR or a standard output that is no terminal gives frames with no escape byte unless --ansi; an --interval outside 1 to 300 or a --count below 1 exits 2

gates.question: What does kbmon do on a Windows console where virtual terminal processing cannot be turned on?

ask: Does the Windows console honour ANSI escape sequences from Python print, or must virtual terminal processing be enabled with SetConsoleMode?
Which ANSI escape sequences clear the screen and move the cursor to the top left?

notes: Plan 2026-10-18: curses is not on Windows, so the view is ANSI with ctypes for the console mode. No host of this project runs the Windows console in a check: the planted enable_vt() case and the review stand in for it. Layout (operator's spec, 2026-10-18; the worker writes it into kb/_self/monitoring.md). W = columns - 1, the last column never written. Rows: [alert line], header, blank, panels kb coord sessions querylog host sprint with a blank between, then the log tail filling the rest (at least 3 lines; rows that do not fit are cut at the bottom). Header: `kbmon · YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SSZ · refresh Ns · frame n · root` (space U+00B7 space, UTC, root `.` for the clone, kbmon bold). Title at column 0: `name  state  S.Ss`; a state other than ok adds `  — reason` and has no body; name bold, state coloured, the rest dim when not ok. Body: columns 0-1 a gutter (`  ` plain, `! ` warning in yellow, `!!` error in red); label at column 2 padded to 10, value at column 12; lists joined by ` · `; tables with a lowercase header row, 2-space gaps, flags by the gutter. Colours (16 ANSI plus bold, each run ends in SGR 0): 32 ok, passed, bars under 80%; 33 warning, timeout, `! ` rows, bars 80-99%; 31 error, `!!` rows, bars at 100%+; 1;97;41 the alert line only; 90 dim (absent, unsupported, reasons); 1 bold names; colour never carries meaning alone. Narrow, in this order: under 100 columns side blocks stack (coord events under the claims, host ceiling as 3 rows); ` · ` lists wrap at an item, continuing at column 12; tables shrink gaps 2 to 1, cut paths from the left as `…/`, then drop the lowest column (sessions: session, then age); free text is cut at W with `…`; ids, counts and states are never cut. Glyphs: ASCII plus · — – …. The alert line is in the alert story's notes, each panel's rows in its own story's notes. Each panel module renders its own body rows; the log title shows absent until mon_log.py lands.
